blocks.h2: Why Sewer Lines Fail in Skokie
blocks.intro: Skokie grew from about 15,000 people in 1950 to nearly 60,000 in 1960. Nearly 2 in 3 homes here were built between 1940 and 1969.

items.body: Clay pipe from the postwar boom has joints every few feet, and decades of roots have pried many of them open.

items.h3: Cast Iron That Scales and Splits
items.body: Cast iron under the basement floor rusts from the inside and can crack along the bottom.

items.h3: Parkway Trees Planted With the Subdivisions
items.body: The trees that line Skokie's blocks are now big enough to send roots into every gap.
Many lines have been dug up and fixed in one spot already, leaving joints between different materials.

blocks.h2: How We Repair a Sewer Line
blocks.intro: Once we know what's wrong, there's usually more than one way to fix it. Which method makes sense depends on the pipe's condition, location, and how it failed.
head: Method
What It Involves
Typical Disruption
rows: A resin-coated liner is pulled through the existing pipe and cured in place, creating a new pipe inside the old one.
Minimal digging, usually just small access points
A new pipe is pulled through the old one while a bursting head fractures the old pipe outward to make room.
Minimal digging, works even when the old pipe is badly damaged
The damaged section is dug up and replaced directly.
More digging, but sometimes the only option depending on damage location and access
blocks.note: Skokie laterals often run under a front walk, a parkway tree and the street curb. The footage shows us which repair keeps the disruption smallest.

blocks.h2: Sewer Repair Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: My home is from the 1950s. Does the whole sewer line need replacing?
items.answer: Not always. Some lines from that era need one section fixed, and others are failing end to end. A [camera inspection](/skokie/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows which one you have.

items.q: Can roots really break a sewer pipe?
items.preview: Yes. They pry joints open and crack old clay.
items.answer: Yes. Roots grow into small gaps, thicken over time and can pry joints apart or crack old clay. That's why they keep coming back after rodding.

items.q: Is lining a good option for old clay pipe?
items.preview: Often, if the pipe still holds its shape.
items.answer: Often. If the clay is cracked but still round, a [trenchless liner](/skokie/trenchless-sewer-repair) can seal it from the inside without a long trench.

items.q: Who fixes the part of the line under the street?
items.preview: It depends on where the problem is.
items.answer: Homeowners are usually responsible for the line from the house to the public sewer. We'll show you on camera where the problem is, so you know who handles it.

items.q: How long does a sewer repair take in Skokie?
items.answer: A spot repair is often done in a day. Larger jobs take a day or two.

items.q: How much does sewer repair cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on the damage, depth and method. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what the camera shows, how deep the pipe is, the repair method and what's above it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before any work.
